title: Episode 24: Five Games to Get / Get Back to the Table
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TDOWMduvE1o

A short, honest episode of intentions. Daniel (@dungeondive) names five games he means to play soon — two never learned, three revisited — and the through-line is a man arguing with his own reluctance.

*Bloodborne: The Board Game* is a re-evaluation. He was negative about it, largely over the timer, which he read as an arbitrary game-over state patched onto a video game that has no such thing. But he liked the moment-to-moment combat enough to want to meet the game on its own terms.

*Robinson Crusoe* and *Nemo's War* are the unlearned pair, and he's candid about why: both are notoriously demanding, he doesn't consider himself a strong board gamer, and the obstacle is mental rather than practical. *Nemo's War* attracts him for reasons he can't name — possibly just the nautical look.

*Iron Helm* he liked without loving; the Iron Chest expansion adds the thematic texture he felt was missing, plus more of Jason Glover's art.

*Fortune and Glory* is the coffin-box he wants back for its pulp Indiana Jones feel — while quietly worrying that his tolerance for fiddly minutiae has thinned since he put it in his top 50.

----

Which intimidating game have you owned longest without learning, and what would it take to break the deadlock?
